summary: Rogue is the foundational terminal dungeon crawler that gave the roguelike genre its name, preserved through original Unix lineage, Epyx ports, and modern source/port packages.

entries.title: Rogue
entries.definitive_edition: Original Unix lineage if available; Epyx/PC port as labeled access route

emulation.emulator: Terminal/Unix environment or DOSBox depending on version
emulation.notes: Version provenance matters more than visual fidelity.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Documented original/early Rogue version with terminal and save policy recorded

primary.version: Original Unix lineage or Epyx Rogue route, recorded by version
primary.why: Rogue's archive value depends on exact version lineage: the original Unix terminal game is the genre origin, while Epyx/PC ports are more accessible. Runs must record version, terminal/display, random seed if available, and whether permadeath/save-scumming is excluded.
primary.how_to_play: Use a preserved Unix/Unix-like Rogue build or an official/known PC port. Record version/source, terminal/emulator, controls, dungeon level, character state, death/win state, seed if available, and save policy.

secondary.why: The original Unix route is the genre-origin target.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record exact build/version and terminal/display behavior.
